#      (CLI -> Trigger, incl. pc symbol resolution + icount defaults), the
#      trigger->argv mapping (plan-test), and the new CLI flags (cli-test).
#   2. validation error paths via the real binary, all exiting BEFORE any spawn:
#      missing ELF, pc without boundaries, an undefined pc symbol, simpoint
#      (F11, not yet), and an unknown trigger.
#   3. real handoff + golden parity (guarded): run csr/pc/icount through both
#      ./hsim (the Python golden) and andes-sim and assert identical window
#      cycle numbers, plus the new output format. Skipped when the qemu/vsim/
#      plugin artifacts or the golden driver are not built.
#
# pc uses handoff_roundtrip.elf's own csr markers as the boundaries (_start =
# the enter marker 0x100000, 0x10000c = the exit marker), so pc reproduces csr's
# switch points exactly -- and exercises BOTH symbol and 0x resolution.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

BIN="$ROOT/build/andes-sim"
ELF="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/handoff_roundtrip.elf"  # asm fixture
CELF="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/rt_c_matmul.elf"       # C fixture (needs shared mmap)
SPIN="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/icount_spin.elf"
ENG=verilator:ax45mpv_premium  # the engine ./hsim resolves by default

bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"

# 1. unit tests (the F9 pure cores)
for t in elf-syms hybrid plan cli; do
  "$ROOT/build/driver/andes-sim-$t-test" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
    || fail "unit test andes-sim-$t-test failed"
done
echo "[ok] unit: elf-syms, hybrid_trigger, trigger->argv (plan), CLI flags"

# 2. validation error paths -- real binary, but every case errors before a spawn
# expect WANT_RC REGEX -- cmd...: run cmd, assert exit code + combined-output match
expect() {
  local want="$1" re="$2"; shift 2
  local out rc
  out=$("$@" 2>&1 </dev/null); rc=$?
  [ "$rc" -eq "$want" ] || fail "rc=$rc want $want for [$*]: $out"
  printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -Eq "$re" || fail "missing /$re/ for [$*]: $out"
}
expect 2 'ELF not found'        "$BIN" run --model hybrid /no/such.elf
expect 2 'engine args go after' "$BIN" run --model hybrid a.elf b.elf
expect 2 'requires --pc-start'  "$BIN" run --model hybrid --trigger pc "$ELF"
expect 2 'not defined' "$BIN" run --model hybrid --trigger pc \
  --pc-start nope_xyz --pc-end _start "$ELF"
expect 2 'F11'              "$BIN" run --model hybrid --trigger simpoint "$ELF"
expect 2 'unknown trigger'  "$BIN" run --model hybrid --trigger bogus "$ELF"
expect 2 'csr or pc'        "$BIN" run --model hybrid --trigger icount \
  --kanata /tmp/k "$SPIN"
expect 2 'requires --kanata' "$BIN" run --model hybrid --trigger csr \
  --objdump /tmp/o "$ELF"
echo "[ok] validation: missing ELF, pc boundaries, bad symbol, simpoint/unknown trigger, kanata/objdump"

# 3. real handoff + golden parity (guarded on built artifacts)
QEMU="$ROOT/build/qemu/qemu-system-riscv64"
SIM="$ROOT/verilator/build/sim_ax45mpv_premium"
PLUGIN="$ROOT/qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so"
if [ -x "$QEMU" ] && [ -x "$SIM" ] && [ -f "$PLUGIN" ] && [ -x "$ROOT/hsim" ]; then
  # Pull the window/kernel cycle integer from either driver's "] N  (vsim..."
  # line (golden csr/pc say "kernel_cycles", icount/andes say "window_cycles";
  # the number's position is identical).
  cyc() { grep -oE '\] [0-9]+  \(' | grep -oE '[0-9]+' | head -1; }
  check_parity() {  # LABEL GOLDEN_NUM ANDES_NUM
    [ -n "$2" ] || fail "$1: golden produced no cycle number"
    [ -n "$3" ] || fail "$1: andes-sim produced no cycle number"
    [ "$2" = "$3" ] || fail "$1: cycle mismatch golden=$2 andes=$3"
    echo "[ok] $1 parity: $3 cycles (golden == andes-sim)"
  }

  # csr -- also assert the new output format (window_cycles + PASS line)
  GO=$(cd "$ROOT" && timeout 180 ./hsim run --mode csr "$ELF" 2>&1 | cyc)
  AO=$(timeout 180 "$BIN" run --model hybrid --trigger csr --engine "$ENG" "$ELF" 2>&1)
  printf '%s\n' "$AO" | grep -Eq '^\[csr window_cycles\] [0-9]+  \(vsim mcycle=' \
    || fail "csr: missing window_cycles line: $AO"
  printf '%s\n' "$AO" | grep -Eq '^PASS: --model hybrid --trigger csr ' \
    || fail "csr: missing PASS line: $AO"
  check_parity csr "$GO" "$(printf '%s\n' "$AO" | cyc)"

  # csr on a C fixture -- the stack/heap + main()'s frame must survive the
  # handoff through the shared mmap (asm fixtures are self-contained; this is
  # the "+ C fixtures" half of the done-when).
  GO=$(cd "$ROOT" && timeout 180 ./hsim run --mode csr "$CELF" 2>&1 | cyc)
  AO=$(timeout 180 "$BIN" run --model hybrid --trigger csr --engine "$ENG" "$CELF" 2>&1 | cyc)
  check_parity csr-c "$GO" "$AO"

  # pc -- symbol start (_start) + 0x end (the exit marker)
  GO=$(cd "$ROOT" && timeout 180 ./hsim run --mode pc \
        --pc-start _start --pc-end 0x10000c "$ELF" 2>&1 | cyc)
  AO=$(timeout 180 "$BIN" run --model hybrid --trigger pc --engine "$ENG" \
        --pc-start _start --pc-end 0x10000c "$ELF" 2>&1 | cyc)
  check_parity pc "$GO" "$AO"

  # icount -- defaults (qemu 10000 / vsim 5000); andes keeps --shared-mem-* but
  # the cycle number is unchanged (this is the deliberate-divergence guard).
  GO=$(cd "$ROOT" && timeout 180 ./hsim run --mode icount "$SPIN" 2>&1 | cyc)
  AO=$(timeout 180 "$BIN" run --model hybrid --trigger icount --engine "$ENG" "$SPIN" 2>&1 | cyc)
  check_parity icount "$GO" "$AO"
else
  echo "[skip] real handoff parity: need built qemu+vsim+plugin and ./hsim"
fi

ok "F9 run --model hybrid (csr|pc|icount)"

echo "[skip] real handoff parity: need built qemu+vsim+plugin and ./hsim"

content.text:
`/simplify → 4 cleanup agents in parallel → apply the fixes`

You are improving the quality of the changed code, not hunting for bugs. Review
it for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude issues, then fix what you
find. Do not look for correctness bugs — that is what `/code-review` is for.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Review (4 cleanup agents in parallel)

Launch **4 independent review agents** via the Agent tool, all in a
single message so they run concurrently. Pass each agent the diff and one of
the four angles below. Each returns its findings with `file`, `line`, a
one-line `summary`, and the concrete cost (what is duplicated, wasted, or
harder to maintain).

### Reuse

Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Name the cheaper alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change is implemented at the right depth, not as a fragile
bandaid. Special cases layered on shared infrastructure are a sign the fix
isn't deep enough — prefer generalizing the underlying mechanism over adding
special cases.

## Phase 2 — Apply the fixes

Wait for all four agents to complete, dedup findings that point at the same
line or mechanism, and fix each remaining one directly. Skip any finding whose
fix would change intended behavior, require changes well outside the reviewed
diff, or that you judge to be a false positive — note the skip rather than
arguing with it. Finish with a brief summary of what was fixed and what was
skipped (or confirm the code was already clean).
Gathering the diff and launching the 4 cleanup agents in parallel. First the diff scope, then the agents.

content.text:
Analysis complete. I've read the full diff, all six new files, and the supporting context (run_plan.cpp, cmd_run.cpp, engine_registry.cpp), and confirmed fixture sizes (5-56 KB) and that discover_engines() spawns a `--describe` subprocess per Verilator build.

## Verdict: nothing here is worth changing on efficiency grounds.

The startup path is already well-ordered: cheap validations (ELF existence, trigger/pc resolution, vsim-flag combos) run before the expensive `discover_engines()`, discovery is done exactly once and threaded into `run_plan` (no re-discovery), `run_plan` builds ctx/argvs once, and moves are used where they matter (`std::move(vsim_extras)`, `out.push_back(std::move(argv))`). The whole thing is dwarfed by the qemu + Verilator-vsim spawns that follow.

Three things I scrutinized and their realistic assessment:

### 1. `driver/elf_syms.cpp:23-31` - `slurp()` reads whole ELF with triple-buffering
- Summary: reads the entire file through `ostringstream`, then `ss.str()` (copy #1 into `s`), then `buf.assign` (copy #2 into the vector) - on top of the stream's own buffer, so ~3 in-memory copies of the file.
- Cost: for a 5-56 KB fixture, single-digit KB times three = microseconds; page-cached.
- Cheaper: `seekg`/`tellg`/`read` straight into the vector (one alloc, one copy). Or a bounded read (header + section headers + symtab/strtab only) instead of the whole file.
- Worth fixing? No. Reading the whole ELF is justified here - fixtures are tiny, a full slurp is simpler than seeking to four scattered sections, and it is gated to pc-trigger only (csr/icount never call `resolve_pc`). The triple-copy is real waste in the abstract but invisible next to a subprocess spawn.

### 2. `driver/hybrid.cpp:22-24` - `resolve_pc` called twice re-slurps + re-scans the symtab
- Summary: pc-trigger resolves `pc_start` and `pc_end` with two independent `resolve_pc` calls; when both are symbols, the ELF is slurped twice and the symtab scanned twice.
- Cost: 2x a ~50 KB read + 2x a few-hundred-symbol linear scan. Negligible, and only on the pc path with two symbol boundaries (a 0x boundary short-circuits before any read).
- Cheaper: slurp+parse once, do two name lookups.
- Worth fixing? No. Too contained and too cheap to matter.

### 3. `driver/cmd_run.cpp:136 vs 146` - `--mmap-size` parsed *after* `discover_engines()`
- Summary: every other cheap validation (trigger resolution, `vsim_extra_args`) is deliberately placed before discovery "so a bad combo fails fast", but the `parse_size(cli.mmap_size)` check sits *after* `discover_engines()`.
- Cost: a malformed `--mmap-size` (e.g. `64Q`) pays for a full `discover_engines()` - one `--describe` subprocess per Verilator build - before failing. Only on that error path; the success path is unaffected.
- Cheaper: move the `parse_size` block above `discover_engines()`, matching the surrounding fail-fast pattern.
- Worth fixing? Marginal. It is the one ordering inconsistency that contradicts the code's own stated principle, and the fix is a trivial block move, but it only bites a rare typo path. Take it or leave it.

No copies of large buffers across call boundaries, no redundant discovery, no sequential work that could overlap (the qemu->vsim legs are inherently ordered - vsim resumes from qemu's drain), and no work added to a genuine hot loop (this is a one-shot CLI).

    [ "$2" = "$3" ] || fail "$1: cycle mismatch golden=$2 andes=$3"
    echo "[ok] $1 parity: $3 cycles (golden == andes-sim)"
  }

  # csr -- also assert the new output format (window_cycles + PASS line)
  GO=$(cd "$ROOT" && timeout 180 ./hsim run --mode csr "$ELF" 2>&1 | cyc)
  AO=$(timeout 180 "$BIN" run --model hybrid --trigger csr --engine "$ENG" "$ELF" 2>&1)
  printf '%s\n' "$AO" | grep -Eq '^\[csr window_cycles\] [0-9]+  \(vsim mcycle=' \
    || fail "csr: missing window_cycles line: $AO"
  printf '%s\n' "$AO" | grep -Eq '^PASS: --model hybrid --trigger csr ' \
    || fail "csr: missing PASS line: $AO"
  check_parity csr "$GO" "$(printf '%s\n' "$AO" | cyc)"

  # csr on a C fixture -- the stack/heap + main()'s frame must survive the
  # handoff through the shared mmap (asm fixtures are self-contained; this is
  # the "+ C fixtures" half of the done-when).
  GO=$(cd "$ROOT" && timeout 180 ./hsim run --mode csr "$CELF" 2>&1 | cyc)
  AO=$(timeout 180 "$BIN" run --model hybrid --trigger csr --engine "$ENG" "$CELF" 2>&1 | cyc)
  check_parity csr-c "$GO" "$AO"

  # pc -- symbol start (_start) + 0x end (the exit marker)
  GO=$(cd "$ROOT" && timeout 180 ./hsim run --mode pc \
        --pc-start _start --pc-end 0x10000c "$ELF" 2>&1 | cyc)
  AO=$(timeout 180 "$BIN" run --model hybrid --trigger pc --engine "$ENG" \
        --pc-start _start --pc-end 0x10000c "$ELF" 2>&1 | cyc)
  check_parity pc "$GO" "$AO"

  # icount -- defaults (qemu 10000 / vsim 5000); andes keeps --shared-mem-* but
  # the cycle number is unchanged (this is the deliberate-divergence guard).
  GO=$(cd "$ROOT" && timeout 180 ./hsim run --mode icount "$SPIN" 2>&1 | cyc)
  AO=$(timeout 180 "$BIN" run --model hybrid --trigger icount --engine "$ENG" "$SPIN" 2>&1 | cyc)
  check_parity icount "$GO" "$AO"

  # kanata ROI trace forwards onto the vsim leg and writes a non-empty file.
  KAN=$(mktemp); rm -f "$KAN"
  timeout 180 "$BIN" run --model hybrid --trigger csr --engine "$ENG" \
    --kanata "$KAN" "$ELF" >/dev/null 2>&1
  [ -s "$KAN" ] || fail "kanata: trace file empty/missing after csr run"
  echo "[ok] kanata: csr run wrote a non-empty ROI trace ($(wc -l <"$KAN") lines)"
  rm -f "$KAN"

fi

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# F8 contract: `run --model accurate` -- one cycle-accurate engine alone, from
# reset (no QEMU, no --resume-from-qemu), transparent passthrough. Layers:
#
#   1. run-test (unit, fast): resolve_accurate_engine's selection branches
#      (default-sole / explicit / ambiguous / missing / wrong-kind) + the F7
#      passthrough_argv assembly. Pure, no spawn.
#   2. fake-engine resolution + exec (no real vsim): a handful of throwaway
#      "engine" scripts that answer `--describe` with JSON and echo a marker
#      when run. Drives the real discover -> resolve -> run_standalone -> exec
#      path end to end. Proves the done-when "selecting a different built <cfg>
#      runs the other binary" deterministically, plus every error path. The
#      fakes ship the SAME standalone template real vsim does ({bin} {elf}), so
#      this exercises the exact argv path.
#   3. real vsim (guarded, best-effort): if a sim_<cfg> is built, invoke it
#      from reset and look for its native "N cycles simulated" line. Standalone
#      from-reset of a hybrid-oriented fixture is environment-dependent, so a
#      timeout or a missing cycle line is a skip, not a failure -- layer 2 is
#      the deterministic proof.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

BIN="$ROOT/build/andes-sim"
RUNTEST="$ROOT/build/driver/andes-sim-run-test"

bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"

# 1. unit: resolution branches + passthrough argv
[ -x "$RUNTEST" ] || fail "missing unit-test binary: $RUNTEST"
"$RUNTEST" || fail "run unit tests (resolve_accurate_engine, passthrough_argv) failed"

# --- fixtures: throwaway engine scripts in a scanned dir --------------------
TMP=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT

# mkengine DIR FILE ID KIND MARKER: a fake engine that self-describes as KIND
# and, when run standalone, echoes RAN:MARKER so we can see which binary ran.
mkengine() {
  local f="$1/$2"
  cat >"$f" <<EOF
#!/bin/sh
if [ "\$1" = "--describe" ]; then
  printf '%s\n' '{"id":"$3","type":"verilator","kind":"$4","roles":["standalone","accurate-leg"],"invoke":{"standalone":["{bin}","{elf}"]}}'
else
  echo "RAN:$5 args:\$*"
fi
EOF
  chmod +x "$f"
}

D1="$TMP/one"; D2="$TMP/two"; DF="$TMP/func"; DE="$TMP/empty"
mkdir -p "$D1" "$D2" "$DF" "$DE"
mkengine "$D1" v1 "verilator:v1" cycle-accurate m1
mkengine "$D2" v1 "verilator:v1" cycle-accurate m1
mkengine "$D2" v2 "verilator:v2" cycle-accurate m2
mkengine "$DF" f0 "verilator:f0" functional    fm

# expect WANT_RC REGEX -- cmd...: run cmd, assert exit code + combined-output match
expect() {
  local want="$1" re="$2"; shift 2
  local out rc
  out=$("$@" 2>&1 </dev/null); rc=$?
  [ "$rc" -eq "$want" ] || fail "rc=$rc want $want for [$*]: $out"
  echo "$out" | grep -Eq "$re" || fail "missing /$re/ for [$*]: $out"
}

# 2a. default = the sole cycle-accurate engine; it runs with the ELF appended
expect 0 'RAN:m1 args:.*dummy\.elf' \
  env ANDES_SIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D1" "$BIN" run --model accurate dummy.elf
# 2b. two cycle-accurate engines, no --engine: ambiguous, names both
expect 2 'multiple cycle-accurate.*verilator:v1.*verilator:v2' \
  env ANDES_SIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D2" "$BIN" run --model accurate dummy.elf
# 2c. explicit --engine picks the named binary (different <cfg> runs the other)
expect 0 'RAN:m1' \
  env ANDES_SIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D2" "$BIN" run --model accurate --engine verilator:v1 dummy.elf
expect 0 'RAN:m2' \
  env ANDES_SIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D2" "$BIN" run --model accurate --engine verilator:v2 dummy.elf
# 2d. no cycle-accurate engine discoverable (qemu is functional): clear error
expect 2 'no cycle-accurate engine' \
  env ANDES_SIM_ENGINES_DIR="$DE" "$BIN" run --model accurate dummy.elf
# 2e. --engine names a functional engine: wrong kind for accurate
expect 2 'cycle-accurate' \
  env ANDES_SIM_ENGINES_DIR="$DF" "$BIN" run --model accurate --engine verilator:f0 dummy.elf
# 2f. --engine matches nothing discovered
expect 2 "no engine 'verilator:nope'" \
  env ANDES_SIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D1" "$BIN" run --model accurate --engine verilator:nope dummy.elf
# 2g. the shared standalone spine still rejects a missing ELF / extra positional
expect 2 'missing ELF' \
  env ANDES_SIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D1" "$BIN" run --model accurate
expect 2 'engine args go after --' \
  env ANDES_SIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D1" "$BIN" run --model accurate a.elf b.elf
# 2h. a CLI arg error is reported before (and instead of) engine discovery:
# missing ELF wins even when no engine exists, rather than "no cycle-accurate
# engine" -- so a typo never pays for a --describe subprocess per build.
expect 2 'missing ELF' \
  env ANDES_SIM_ENGINES_DIR="$DE" "$BIN" run --model accurate
echo "[ok] fake-engine resolution + standalone exec (all branches)"

# 3. real vsim (guarded, best-effort)
SIM=$(ls "$ROOT"/verilator/build/sim_* 2>/dev/null | head -1)
ELF="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/handoff_roundtrip.elf"
if [ -n "$SIM" ] && [ -x "$SIM" ] && [ -f "$ELF" ]; then
  ID=$("$SIM" --describe 2>/dev/null | sed -nE 's/.*"id"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"([^"]+)".*/\1/p' | head -1)
  # The current fixtures are hybrid-oriented and loop forever standalone (no
  # exit path without QEMU's semihosting), so this caps the attempt: a cycle
  # line confirms the done-when; a timeout (rc 124) only confirms vsim launched
  # and is running, which is still useful. Either way -> not a failure. The cap
  # is short: the cycle line, if it comes, comes right after launch; otherwise
  # we are just confirming launch, so there is no point waiting longer.
  out=$(timeout 10 "$BIN" run --model accurate ${ID:+--engine "$ID"} "$ELF" 2>&1 </dev/null); rc=$?
  if echo "$out" | grep -Eq "[0-9]+ cycles simulated"; then
    echo "[ok] real accurate: vsim ran '$ELF' from reset, printed its cycle line (rc=$rc)"
  elif [ "$rc" -eq 124 ]; then
    echo "[skip] real accurate: vsim launched but did not finish in 10s (expected: standalone-from-reset of a hybrid fixture has no exit path)"
  else
    echo "[skip] real accurate: vsim exited rc=$rc with no cycle line (standalone-from-reset of a hybrid fixture is env-dependent)"
  fi
else
  echo "[skip] real accurate run: no built sim_* and/or fixture ($SIM / $ELF)"
fi

ok "F8 run --model accurate"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# F8 contract: `run --model accurate` -- one cycle-accurate engine alone, from
# reset (no QEMU, no --resume-from-qemu), transparent passthrough. Layers:
#
#   1. run-test (unit, fast): resolve_accurate_engine's selection branches
#      (default-sole / explicit / ambiguous / missing / wrong-kind) + the F7
#      passthrough_argv assembly. Pure, no spawn.
#   2. fake-engine resolution + exec (no real vsim): a handful of throwaway
#      "engine" scripts that answer `--describe` with JSON and echo a marker
#      when run. Drives the real discover -> resolve -> run_standalone -> exec
#      path end to end. Proves the done-when "selecting a different built <cfg>
#      runs the other binary" deterministically, plus every error path. The
#      fakes ship the SAME standalone template real vsim does ({bin} {elf}), so
#      this exercises the exact argv path.
#   3. real vsim (guarded, best-effort): if a sim_<cfg> is built, invoke it
#      from reset and look for its native "N cycles simulated" line. Standalone
#      from-reset of a hybrid-oriented fixture is environment-dependent, so a
#      timeout or a missing cycle line is a skip, not a failure -- layer 2 is
#      the deterministic proof.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

BIN="$ROOT/build/andes-sim"
RUNTEST="$ROOT/build/driver/andes-sim-run-test"

bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"

# 1. unit: resolution branches + passthrough argv
[ -x "$RUNTEST" ] || fail "missing unit-test binary: $RUNTEST"
"$RUNTEST" || fail "run unit tests (resolve_accurate_engine, passthrough_argv) failed"

# --- fixtures: throwaway engine scripts in a scanned dir --------------------
TMP=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT

# mkengine DIR FILE ID KIND MARKER: a fake engine that self-describes as KIND
# and, when run standalone, echoes RAN:MARKER so we can see which binary ran.
mkengine() {
  local f="$1/$2"
  cat >"$f" <<EOF
#!/bin/sh
if [ "\$1" = "--describe" ]; then
  printf '%s\n' '{"id":"$3","type":"verilator","kind":"$4","roles":["standalone","accurate-leg"],"invoke":{"standalone":["{bin}","{elf}"]}}'
else
  echo "RAN:$5 args:\$*"
fi
EOF
  chmod +x "$f"
}

D1="$TMP/one"; D2="$TMP/two"; DF="$TMP/func"; DE="$TMP/empty"
mkdir -p "$D1" "$D2" "$DF" "$DE"
mkengine "$D1" v1 "verilator:v1" cycle-accurate m1
mkengine "$D2" v1 "verilator:v1" cycle-accurate m1
mkengine "$D2" v2 "verilator:v2" cycle-accurate m2
mkengine "$DF" f0 "verilator:f0" functional    fm

# expect: assert rc + output regex (shared helper from tests/lib/log.sh)

# 2a. default = the sole cycle-accurate engine; it runs with the ELF appended
expect 0 'RAN:m1 args:.*dummy\.elf' \
  env ANDES_SIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D1" "$BIN" run --model accurate dummy.elf
# 2b. two cycle-accurate engines, no --engine: ambiguous, names both
expect 2 'multiple cycle-accurate.*verilator:v1.*verilator:v2' \
  env ANDES_SIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D2" "$BIN" run --model accurate dummy.elf
# 2c. explicit --engine picks the named binary (different <cfg> runs the other)
expect 0 'RAN:m1' \
  env ANDES_SIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D2" "$BIN" run --model accurate --engine verilator:v1 dummy.elf
expect 0 'RAN:m2' \
  env ANDES_SIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D2" "$BIN" run --model accurate --engine verilator:v2 dummy.elf
# 2d. no cycle-accurate engine discoverable (qemu is functional): clear error
expect 2 'no cycle-accurate engine' \
  env ANDES_SIM_ENGINES_DIR="$DE" "$BIN" run --model accurate dummy.elf
# 2e. --engine names a functional engine: wrong kind for accurate
expect 2 'cycle-accurate' \
  env ANDES_SIM_ENGINES_DIR="$DF" "$BIN" run --model accurate --engine verilator:f0 dummy.elf
# 2f. --engine matches nothing discovered
expect 2 "no engine 'verilator:nope'" \
  env ANDES_SIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D1" "$BIN" run --model accurate --engine verilator:nope dummy.elf
# 2g. the shared standalone spine still rejects a missing ELF / extra positional
expect 2 'missing ELF' \

expect 2 'missing ELF' \
  env ANDES_SIM_ENGINES_DIR="$DE" "$BIN" run --model accurate
echo "[ok] fake-engine resolution + standalone exec (all branches)"

# 3. real vsim (guarded, best-effort)

  # The current fixtures are hybrid-oriented and loop forever standalone (no
  # exit path without QEMU's semihosting), so this caps the attempt: a cycle
  # line confirms the done-when; a timeout (rc 124) only confirms vsim launched
  # and is running, which is still useful. Either way -> not a failure. The cap
  # is short: the cycle line, if it comes, comes right after launch; otherwise
  # we are just confirming launch, so there is no point waiting longer.
  out=$(timeout 10 "$BIN" run --model accurate ${ID:+--engine "$ID"} "$ELF" 2>&1 </dev/null); rc=$?

  elif [ "$rc" -eq 124 ]; then

else

fi

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# F9 contract: `run --model hybrid` -- orchestrate a QEMU1 -> vsim handoff (no
# QEMU2) and print the one-line window-cycle figure for the csr | pc | icount
# triggers. Three layers:
#
#   1. unit (fast, no spawn): the elf-syms boundary resolver, hybrid_trigger
#      (CLI -> Trigger, incl. pc symbol resolution + icount defaults), the
#      trigger->argv mapping (plan-test), and the new CLI flags (cli-test).
#   2. validation error paths via the real binary, all exiting BEFORE any spawn:
#      missing ELF, pc without boundaries, an undefined pc symbol, simpoint
#      (F11, not yet), and an unknown trigger.
#   3. real handoff + golden parity (guarded): run csr/pc/icount through both
#      ./hsim (the Python golden) and andes-sim and assert identical window
#      cycle numbers, plus the new output format. Skipped when the qemu/vsim/
#      plugin artifacts or the golden driver are not built.
#
# pc uses handoff_roundtrip.elf's own csr markers as the boundaries (_start =
# the enter marker 0x100000, 0x10000c = the exit marker), so pc reproduces csr's
# switch points exactly -- and exercises BOTH symbol and 0x resolution.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

BIN="$ROOT/build/andes-sim"
ELF="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/handoff_roundtrip.elf"  # asm fixture
CELF="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/rt_c_matmul.elf"       # C fixture (needs shared mmap)
SPIN="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/icount_spin.elf"
ENG=verilator:ax45mpv_premium  # the engine ./hsim resolves by default

bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"

# 1. unit tests (the F9 pure cores)
for t in elf-syms hybrid plan cli; do
  "$ROOT/build/driver/andes-sim-$t-test" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
    || fail "unit test andes-sim-$t-test failed"
done
echo "[ok] unit: elf-syms, hybrid_trigger, trigger->argv (plan), CLI flags"

# 2. validation error paths -- real binary, but every case errors before a spawn
# (expect: assert rc + output regex; shared helper from tests/lib/log.sh)
expect 2 'ELF not found'        "$BIN" run --model hybrid /no/such.elf
expect 2 'engine args go after' "$BIN" run --model hybrid a.elf b.elf
expect 2 'requires --pc-start'  "$BIN" run --model hybrid --trigger pc "$ELF"
expect 2 'not defined' "$BIN" run --model hybrid --trigger pc \
  --pc-start nope_xyz --pc-end _start "$ELF"
expect 2 'F11'              "$BIN" run --model hybrid --trigger simpoint "$ELF"
expect 2 'unknown trigger'  "$BIN" run --model hybrid --trigger bogus "$ELF"
expect 2 'csr or pc'        "$BIN" run --model hybrid --trigger icount \
  --kanata /tmp/k "$SPIN"
expect 2 'requires --kanata' "$BIN" run --model hybrid --trigger csr \
  --objdump /tmp/o "$ELF"
echo "[ok] validation: missing ELF, pc boundaries, bad symbol, simpoint/unknown trigger, kanata/objdump"

# 3. real handoff + golden parity (guarded on built artifacts)
QEMU="$ROOT/build/qemu/qemu-system-riscv64"
SIM="$ROOT/verilator/build/sim_ax45mpv_premium"
PLUGIN="$ROOT/qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so"
if [ -x "$QEMU" ] && [ -x "$SIM" ] && [ -f "$PLUGIN" ] && [ -x "$ROOT/hsim" ]; then
  # Pull the window/kernel cycle integer from either driver's "] N  (vsim..."
  # line (golden csr/pc say "kernel_cycles", icount/andes say "window_cycles";
  # the number's position is identical).
  cyc() { grep -oE '\] [0-9]+  \(' | grep -oE '[0-9]+' | head -1; }
  check_parity() {  # LABEL GOLDEN_NUM ANDES_NUM
    [ -n "$2" ] || fail "$1: golden produced no cycle number"
    [ -n "$3" ] || fail "$1: andes-sim produced no cycle number"
    [ "$2" = "$3" ] || fail "$1: cycle mismatch golden=$2 andes=$3"
    echo "[ok] $1 parity: $3 cycles (golden == andes-sim)"
  }

  # csr -- also assert the new output format (window_cycles + PASS line)
  GO=$(cd "$ROOT" && timeout 180 ./hsim run --mode csr "$ELF" 2>&1 | cyc)
  AO=$(timeout 180 "$BIN" run --model hybrid --trigger csr --engine "$ENG" "$ELF" 2>&1)
  printf '%s\n' "$AO" | grep -Eq '^\[csr window_cycles\] [0-9]+  \(vsim mcycle=' \
    || fail "csr: missing window_cycles line: $AO"
  printf '%s\n' "$AO" | grep -Eq '^PASS: --model hybrid --trigger csr ' \
    || fail "csr: missing PASS line: $AO"
  check_parity csr "$GO" "$(printf '%s\n' "$AO" | cyc)"

  # csr on a C fixture -- the stack/heap + main()'s frame must survive the
  # handoff through the shared mmap (asm fixtures are self-contained; this is
  # the "+ C fixtures" half of the done-when).
  GO=$(cd "$ROOT" && timeout 180 ./hsim run --mode csr "$CELF" 2>&1 | cyc)
  AO=$(timeout 180 "$BIN" run --model hybrid --trigger csr --engine "$ENG" "$CELF" 2>&1 | cyc)
  check_parity csr-c "$GO" "$AO"

  # pc -- symbol start (_start) + 0x end (the exit marker)
  GO=$(cd "$ROOT" && timeout 180 ./hsim run --mode pc \
        --pc-start _start --pc-end 0x10000c "$ELF" 2>&1 | cyc)
  AO=$(timeout 180 "$BIN" run --model hybrid --trigger pc --engine "$ENG" \
        --pc-start _start --pc-end 0x10000c "$ELF" 2>&1 | cyc)
  check_parity pc "$GO" "$AO"

  # icount -- defaults (qemu 10000 / vsim 5000); andes keeps --shared-mem-* but
  # the cycle number is unchanged (this is the deliberate-divergence guard).
  GO=$(cd "$ROOT" && timeout 180 ./hsim run --mode icount "$SPIN" 2>&1 | cyc)
  AO=$(timeout 180 "$BIN" run --model hybrid --trigger icount --engine "$ENG" "$SPIN" 2>&1 | cyc)
  check_parity icount "$GO" "$AO"

  # kanata ROI trace forwards onto the vsim leg and writes a non-empty file.
  KAN=$(mktemp); rm -f "$KAN"
  timeout 180 "$BIN" run --model hybrid --trigger csr --engine "$ENG" \
    --kanata "$KAN" "$ELF" >/dev/null 2>&1
  [ -s "$KAN" ] || fail "kanata: trace file empty/missing after csr run"
  echo "[ok] kanata: csr run wrote a non-empty ROI trace ($(wc -l <"$KAN") lines)"
  rm -f "$KAN"
else
  echo "[skip] real handoff parity: need built qemu+vsim+plugin and ./hsim"
fi

ok "F9 run --model hybrid (csr|pc|icount)"

# Shared status printers for test scripts. Sourced (not executed).
#
#   fail <msg...>          -> "[FAIL] <msg>" on stderr, exit 1
#   ok   <msg...>          -> "[ok] <msg>" on stdout
#   expect <rc> <re> CMD.. -> run CMD, fail unless it exits <rc> and its
#                             combined output matches the <re> regex
#
# These patterns were duplicated byte-identically across many test scripts.
# Source via:   . "$SCRIPT_DIR/<rel>/lib/log.sh"

fail() { echo "[FAIL] $*" >&2; exit 1; }
ok()   { echo "[ok] $*"; }

expect() {
  local want="$1" re="$2"; shift 2
  local out rc
  out=$("$@" 2>&1 </dev/null); rc=$?
  [ "$rc" -eq "$want" ] || fail "rc=$rc want $want for [$*]: $out"
  printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -Eq "$re" || fail "missing /$re/ for [$*]: $out"
}

# F9 - `run --model hybrid` (csr | pc | icount triggers)

## Context

F9 is the next ROADMAP feature (F0-F8 done). Today `andes-sim run --model hybrid`
prints `not yet implemented`. The goal: orchestrate a real QEMU1 -> vsim handoff
for the three kernel/window triggers and print the cycle figure - matching the
Python golden `hsim`'s numbers, and replacing its `tests/e2e.sh` delegation.

Good news: **F6 already does the hard part.** `run_plan` (driver/run_plan.cpp)
spawns `[qemu fast-leg -> vsim accurate-leg]`, threads the drained
`hybrid_state_v1`, and reads each leg's `mcycle`. `plan_itest.cpp` proves the
**csr** trigger runs end-to-end and `vsim_mcycle > qemu_mcycle`. So F9 is mostly:
teach the plan the **pc** and **icount** trigger args, port the ELF symbol
lookup, add the CLI flags, and wire `cmd_run` to build+run the plan and print.

Golden behavior I verified directly (real `hsim`, not the hallucinated `hsim.py`):
- QEMU leg (all triggers): `-object memory-backend-file...` + `-plugin {plugin},outfile={state},<trig>`, exits 200. (`hsim:725-755`, `e2e.sh:111-118`)
- vsim leg: `{elf} --resume-from-qemu {in} --handoff-out {out} --shared-mem-{path,size,base} <trig>`, exits 200. (`e2e.sh:134-142`)
- Trigger args: **csr** none; **pc** plugin `,enter_pc=0x<start>` + vsim `--hybrid-exit-pc 0x<end>`; **icount** plugin `,icount=<N>` + vsim `--hybrid-icount <M>`. (`e2e.sh:85-89`, `hsim:275,361`)
- Cycle line: `[<label> window_cycles] <V-Q>  (vsim mcycle=<V> - qemu mcycle=<Q>)`. (`hsim:465`)
- pc boundary = symbol name or `0x` addr, resolved against the ELF symtab. (`tests/lib/roi.sh:15-21`)
- Defaults: qemu-icount 10000, vsim-icount 5000, mmap 128 MiB. (`hsim:1304-1342`)

## Core architecture (the one new idea: trigger -> per-leg argv)

Everything else reuses F6. A trigger contributes args to each leg, **chosen by
the leg's role**:

```
                fast-leg (qemu)                    accurate-leg (vsim)
  csr      (nothing)                          (nothing)
  pc       ,enter_pc=0x<start>  (plugin tok)  --hybrid-exit-pc 0x<end>  (extra tokens)
  icount   ,icount=<N>          (plugin tok)  --hybrid-icount <M>       (extra tokens)
```

Two mechanisms, because QEMU plugin args MUST be a comma-suffix inside the one
`-plugin` token, while vsim args are normal separate tokens:
- **qemu**: a `{trigger}` placeholder folded into the plugin token; the framework
  fills it with the comma-suffix (or `""`).
- **vsim**: extra tokens appended after the filled template.

New pure helper `leg_trigger_args(Trigger, role) -> {plugin_suffix, extra[]}` in
`run_plan.{hpp,cpp}`. `plan_argvs` calls it per step: sets `ctx["trigger"] =
plugin_suffix`, then appends `extra[]` after `build_argv`.

**Why framework-side, not in `--describe`:** the engine contract lists trigger
*names* only (`triggers: [...]`); the canonical flag spellings are framework
knowledge - the same ones the Python golden hardcodes. A per-trigger argv
template in `--describe` is a later purist extension, not F9.

User-forwarded vsim extras (`--vsim-warmup-icount`, later `--kanata`) are NOT
trigger args: add a `Step.extra_args` field, appended last by `plan_argvs`.

## Increments (strict TDD: one failing test -> minimal code -> next)

**1. ELF symbol resolver** - new `driver/elf_syms.{hpp,cpp}` + `elf_syms_test.cpp`.
   `resolve_pc(elf, boundary, &err) -> bare-hex string`. `0x<h>`/`0X<h>` -> `<h>`
   verbatim; else read the ELF `.symtab` directly via `<elf.h>` (`Elf64_Ehdr/Shdr/Sym`,
   find `SHT_SYMTAB` + its strtab, match name -> `st_value`); unknown symbol ->
   `""` + err. Port of `tests/lib/roi.sh:resolve_pc`, but reading the symtab in
   C++ (no `nm` shell-out), per the ROADMAP. RED: 0x passthrough, a known symbol
   from a built fixture, unknown-symbol error.

**2. Trigger -> argv** - extend `plan_argvs` + `plan_test.cpp`. Add
   `leg_trigger_args`; change the builtin_qemu fast-leg plugin token
   `"{plugin},outfile={state_out}"` -> `"...{state_out}{trigger}"`
   (`engine_registry.cpp:46`); append `Step.extra_args`. RED in plan_test: pc step
   -> qemu argv has `enter_pc=0x..`, vsim argv has `--hybrid-exit-pc 0x..`; icount
   similar; **csr unchanged** (plan_itest stays green).

**3. CLI flags** - extend `Cli` + `parse_cli` + `cli_test.cpp`. Add string fields
   `pc_start, pc_end, qemu_icount, vsim_icount, mmap_size, vsim_warmup_icount`
   (empty = default; reuse the `match_opt` table in `cli.cpp:57-63`).

**4. `cmd_run` hybrid arm** - `driver/cmd_run.cpp` + a pure unit test + an
   acceptance script.
   - 4a (pure, in `run_test.cpp`): `hybrid_trigger(cli, elf, &err) -> Trigger`
     - csr `{}`; pc resolves start/end via `resolve_pc` and stores `enter_pc`/
       `exit_pc` (with `0x`); icount applies the 10000/5000 defaults. RED first.
   - 4b (wire `run_hybrid`): validate one ELF (reuse `check_one_elf`), default
     `--trigger` to `csr`, require `--pc-start`/`--pc-end` for pc; discover
     engines, `resolve_accurate_engine` (reuse, `engine_registry.hpp:42`); build
     the 2-step `Plan` (mmap via `parse_size`, default 128 MiB); set accurate-leg
     `extra_args` for warmup; `run_plan`; on success print a short banner + the
     `window_cycles` line + `PASS`, on failure print the error and return 1.
   - Acceptance `tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_f9.sh`: run csr / pc / icount on
     fixtures, assert the `window_cycles` line and a positive number; pc with a
     **symbol** AND a **0x** boundary. **Parity:** for each, also run
     `./hsim run --mode <m> ...`, extract the integer from
     `] <N>  (vsim mcycle=`, assert equal to andes-sim's.

**5. (stretch, only if 1-4 land clean) `--kanata`/`--objdump` forward** - same
   `Step.extra_args` path: csr/pc only, `--objdump` requires `--kanata`, emit
   `--kanata <f> --kanata-roi [--objdump <f>]` (`e2e.sh:102-107`). Visualization
   only, not in the done-when - deferred if the session is full.

## Key files

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `driver/elf_syms.{hpp,cpp}` | NEW - symtab symbol/0x resolver |
| `driver/elf_syms_test.cpp` | NEW - unit test |
| `driver/run_plan.{hpp,cpp}` | `leg_trigger_args`; `plan_argvs` applies trigger + `extra_args` |
| `driver/plan.hpp` | `Step.extra_args` field |
| `driver/engine_registry.cpp` | fast-leg plugin token gains `{trigger}` |
| `driver/cli.{hpp,cpp}` | new hybrid flags |
| `driver/cmd_run.cpp` | `run_hybrid` + `hybrid_trigger` |
| `driver/CMakeLists.txt` | add `elf_syms.cpp` to `andes-sim`; new `elf-syms-test`; add `elf_syms.cpp` to run-test target |
| `driver/{plan,cli,run}_test.cpp` | new cases |
| `tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_f9.sh` | NEW - acceptance + parity |
| `driver/ROADMAP.md` | F9 State -> DONE |

## Reuse (no reinvention)
`run_plan`/`plan_argvs`/`build_argv` (F6), `resolve_accurate_engine` +
`builtin_qemu` (engine_registry.hpp), `parse_size` (shm.hpp), `check_one_elf`
(cmd_run.cpp), `read_state_file` (state.hpp), `match_opt` (cli.cpp).

## Verification
- Build: `bash scripts/build_driver.sh`
- Unit: `./build/andes-sim-elf-syms-test && ./build/andes-sim-plan-test && ./build/andes-sim-cli-test && ./build/andes-sim-run-test` (all print `... OK`)
- Integration (real qemu+vsim): `./build/andes-sim-plan-itest` (csr still green)
- Acceptance + parity: `bash tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_f9.sh`
- Manual smoke:
  `./build/andes-sim run --model hybrid --trigger csr tests/fixtures/handoff_roundtrip.elf`
  `./build/andes-sim run --model hybrid --trigger icount tests/fixtures/icount_spin.elf`

## Notes / one deliberate divergence
- **icount keeps `--shared-mem-*`** (the Python inline path omits them). One
  vsim template serves all triggers; the shared mmap is harmless for asm icount
  fixtures (CLAUDE.md already says asm fixtures use it anyway). The acceptance
  test's icount parity check confirms the cycle number is unchanged; if it
  diverges I'll add a no-mem variant, but I expect a tight loop's mcycle to be
  identical.
- csr/pc output changes from e2e.sh's full log to the one-line window-cycles
  figure (ROADMAP-sanctioned; the number is unchanged).
- No per-leg `--` passthrough and no QEMU2 (both out of scope by design).

skills.content:
`/simplify → 4 cleanup agents in parallel → apply the fixes`

You are improving the quality of the changed code, not hunting for bugs. Review
it for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude issues, then fix what you
find. Do not look for correctness bugs — that is what `/code-review` is for.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Review (4 cleanup agents in parallel)

Launch **4 independent review agents** via the Agent tool, all in a
single message so they run concurrently. Pass each agent the diff and one of
the four angles below. Each returns its findings with `file`, `line`, a
one-line `summary`, and the concrete cost (what is duplicated, wasted, or
harder to maintain).

### Reuse

Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Name the cheaper alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change is implemented at the right depth, not as a fragile
bandaid. Special cases layered on shared infrastructure are a sign the fix
isn't deep enough — prefer generalizing the underlying mechanism over adding
special cases.

## Phase 2 — Apply the fixes

Wait for all four agents to complete, dedup findings that point at the same
line or mechanism, and fix each remaining one directly. Skip any finding whose
fix would change intended behavior, require changes well outside the reviewed
diff, or that you judge to be a false positive — note the skip rather than
arguing with it. Finish with a brief summary of what was fixed and what was
skipped (or confirm the code was already clean).

Based on my systematic exploration of the driver directory, here is the precise map:

## 1. Top-Level Help Text and Command Registry

**Location:** `/home/nick/work/hybrid_sim/driver/main.cpp`, lines 35-62

```cpp
constexpr Subcommand kSubcommands[] = {
    {"build", "build artifacts (qemu, vsim, plugin, simpoint, fixtures, driver)"},
    {"run", "run one simulation (--model fast|accurate|hybrid)"},
    {"test", "run the end-to-end suite"},
    {"list", "list fixtures|models|engines"},
    {"doctor", "check environment health"},
    {"profile", "profile a workload into a basic-block vector"},
    {"cluster", "cluster a BBV into SimPoint phases"},
    {"archive", "snapshot a drained state into a replayable dir"},
    {"replay", "replay a snapshot"},
    {"estimate", "whole-program cycle estimate (run --model hybrid --trigger simpoint)"},
};
```

The top-level description string is at **line 56:**
```cpp
std::fputs("Multi-engine driver for the Andes simulators (QEMU + Verilator).\n\n", out);
```

---

## 2. Command Dispatch Mechanism

**Location:** `/home/nick/work/hybrid_sim/driver/main.cpp`, lines 103-131

Single if-chain dispatch (lines 116-119):
```cpp
if (cli.subcommand == "list") return cmd_list(cli);
if (cli.subcommand == "doctor") return cmd_doctor(cli);
if (cli.subcommand == "build") return cmd_build(cli);
if (cli.subcommand == "run") return cmd_run(cli);
```

Anything not matched falls through to the stub (lines 121-131):
```cpp
// Remaining subcommands stub out until their feature lands...
std::fprintf(stderr, "andes-sim %s: not yet implemented (repo root: %s)\n",
             cli.subcommand.c_str(), root.c_str());
return 3;
```

**Command handlers:**

| Command | Handler | File | Status |
|---------|---------|------|--------|
| list | `cmd_list()` | cmd_list.cpp | Real (F2 discovery) |
| doctor | `cmd_doctor()` | cmd_doctor.cpp | Real (with engine discovery appended) |

- `test` - in command table, no handler in dispatch
- `profile` - in command table, no handler in dispatch
- `cluster` - in command table, no handler in dispatch
- `archive` - in command table, no handler in dispatch
- `replay` - in command table, no handler in dispatch
- `estimate` - in command table, no handler in dispatch

Quote from main.cpp:129:
```cpp
std::fprintf(stderr, "andes-sim %s: not yet implemented (repo root: %s)\n",
             cli.subcommand.c_str(), root.c_str());
```

**Real commands:**
- `build` - executes build steps (cmd_build.cpp, lines 77-102)
- `run` - delegates to `run_fast()`, `run_accurate()`, or `run_hybrid()` (cmd_run.cpp, lines 180-195)
- `list` - enumerates fixtures/models/engines (cmd_list.cpp, lines 170-185)
- `doctor` - health check with engine discovery section appended (cmd_doctor.cpp, lines 286-314)

**All occurrences in non-test source (*.cpp, *.hpp, excluding *_test.cpp/*_itest.cpp):**

| File:Line | Context | Type | Classification |
|-----------|---------|------|-----------------|
| main.cpp:56 | Help text: "Multi-engine driver for the Andes simulators (QEMU + Verilator)." | User-facing help | **Cosmetic label** (appears in `--help` output) |
| main.cpp:73 | Help text for `run --engine`: "(e.g. verilator:ax45mpv_premium)" | User-facing help | **Cosmetic example** (shown in subcommand help, but matches actual engine id format) |
| models.hpp:3 | Comment: "separately (built-in qemu, or a discovered verilator:<cfg>)." | Comment | Informational |
| models.hpp:6 | Comment: "accurate = one Verilator alone..." | Comment | Informational |

| engine_registry.hpp:32 | Comment: "paying none of the Verilator-engine discovery cost." | Comment | Informational |
| engine_registry.cpp:126 | Comment: "The default verilator/build scan passes..." | Comment | Informational |
| engine_registry.cpp:167 | Path: `scan_dir(repo_root() / "verilator" / "build", ...)` | Directory scan logic | **Logic-dependent** (hardcoded scan path, not cosmetic) |
| cmd_doctor.cpp:60 | Path: `root / "verilator" / "build" / "sim_ax45mpv_premium"` | Artifact check | **Logic-dependent** (hardcoded artifact path) |

| cmd_run.cpp:33 | Comment: "per Verilator build" | Comment | Informational |
| cmd_run.cpp:66 | Comment: "per Verilator build" | Comment | Informational |
| cmd_run.cpp:81 | Comment: "discover the Verilator build(s)" | Comment | Informational |
| cmd_run.cpp:85 | Comment: "per Verilator build" | Comment | Informational |
| cmd_run.cpp:123 | Comment: "per Verilator build" | Comment | Informational |

**Summary by classification:**

**Cosmetic labels** (can be renamed without breaking logic):
- Line 56 (main.cpp): Help text
- Line 73 (main.cpp): Engine id example
- Line 23 (models.hpp): `list models` output
- Lines 25-26 (models.hpp): `list models` output

**Logic-dependent** (hardcoded paths/scans; renaming would require code changes):
- Line 167 (engine_registry.cpp): Directory scan path `verilator/build`
- Line 60 (cmd_doctor.cpp): Artifact path `verilator/build/sim_ax45mpv_premium`
- Line 110 (cmd_doctor.cpp): Submodule marker path `verilator/CMakeLists.txt`

**Key finding:** The type field "verilator" itself is **never hardcoded in the driver**. It comes from each engine's JSON descriptor (via `--describe` or sidecar .json). The driver does NOT compare `e.type == "verilator"` anywhere; it only reads and displays the type string. The only logic-dependent references are the filesystem paths `verilator/build` and `verilator/CMakeLists.txt`, which are separate from the user-facing type label.

---

## 5. The `list` Subcommand Details

**Location:** `/home/nick/work/hybrid_sim/driver/cmd_list.cpp`

Three sub-targets:

| Target | Implementation | Output |
|--------|---|---|
| `list fixtures` | `list_fixtures()` lines 109-126 | Parses `tests/fixtures/Makefile`, prints FIXTURE / FAMILY columns |
| `list models` | `list_models()` lines 128-141 | Prints `kModels[]` array, columns: MODEL / ENGINES / NOTES; uses models.hpp values like `"verilator:<cfg>"` |
| `list engines` | `list_engines()` lines 143-166 | Calls `discover_engines()`, prints ENGINE / TYPE / KIND / VLEN / TRIGGERS; engine id includes type prefix like `"verilator:ax45mpv_premium"` |

Engine IDs are formed by the `discover_engines()` function (engine_registry.cpp), which either returns the built-in `{"id": "qemu", ...}` or scans `verilator/build/` for binaries and queries their `--describe` output. The engine descriptor's `id` field (set by the engine's JSON) becomes the printed engine ID (e.g., `verilator:ax45mpv_premium`).

input.content:
# andes-sim release surface: hide "verilator", split release vs dev commands

## Context

`andes-sim` is the release product, but `--help` today exposes implementation
detail and unfinished work. Looking at `./build/andes-sim --help` the user (PM)
asked for four things:

1. Hide the word **verilator** from users (it shows in the `--help` tagline, the
   `--engine` example, `list models`, and the whole `list engines` TYPE column +
   ids like `verilator:ax45mpv_premium`).
2. Don't output **unfinished** features (`estimate`, `cluster`, `profile`, and
   the like).
3. **Separate** release features from development features.
4. The release product **shouldn't include `build` and `test`**.

Today the command table (`driver/main.cpp:35-46`) lists all 10 commands and the
help printer shows every one. Engine identity ("verilator") comes from the vsim
binary's `--describe` JSON; the driver passes it through verbatim. Selection
keys off `kind=="cycle-accurate"`, never the `type` string (`engine_registry.hpp:45`),
so relabeling the engine is safe.

Outcome: a clean release surface (`run`, `list`) that never says "verilator",
with `build`/`test`/`doctor` reachable to developers via an env var, and the
half-built ROADMAP commands hidden until they land.

## Decisions (locked)

- Replace "verilator" with **`vsim`** everywhere on the surface: TYPE column
  `vsim`, ids `vsim:ax45mpv_premium`, `--engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium`.
- Scrub **everywhere incl. ids** (one normalization point at discovery flips
  list / `--engine` / errors / banner together).
- Reveal dev commands via **`ANDES_SIM_DEV=1`** (release `--help` stays clean +
  one hint line; the env var adds a "developer commands" section).

**Inference to confirm at approval:** `doctor` -> **dev tier** (not release). Its
content is entirely build/setup (submodules, toolchain, `./hsim build`) and it is
the only Release command that would still print real `verilator/` paths
(`cmd_doctor.cpp:60,110`) which cannot be renamed. So Release = `run` + `list`.

## Command tiers (the one new idea)

Add `enum class Tier { Release, Dev, Hidden }` + a field on `Subcommand`
(`main.cpp:28-31`). `print_usage` shows Release; appends a Dev section only when
`ANDES_SIM_DEV` is set; Hidden is never listed. Dispatch is unchanged, so the
command surface stays stable (matches the file's stated F0 design intent).

| Tier | Commands | `--help` behavior |
|------|----------|-------------------|
| Release | `run`, `list` | always listed |
| Dev | `build`, `test`, `doctor` | listed only under `ANDES_SIM_DEV=1` |
| Hidden | `profile`, `cluster`, `archive`, `replay`, `estimate` | never listed; explicit invocation still hits the existing "not yet implemented" stub |

Not in dev mode, the release help ends with one hint line:
`(set ANDES_SIM_DEV=1 to show developer commands)`.

## Change A - hide "verilator" -> "vsim"

**Single normalization point.** Add an inline helper in
`driver/engine_registry.hpp` (mirroring the existing inline `resolve_accurate_engine`):

```cpp
inline void normalize_engine_label(EngineDescriptor& d) {
  // The vsim binary self-reports the third-party simulator name; the product
  // surface speaks "vsim". One translation point so every downstream consumer
  // (list / --engine / errors / banner) sees the product id.
  if (d.type == "verilator") d.type = "vsim";
  if (d.id.rfind("verilator:", 0) == 0) d.id = "vsim:" + d.id.substr(10);
}
```

Call it in `engine_registry.cpp` `scan_dir`, right after `describe_one` succeeds
and **before** the `seen.insert(d.id)` dedup, so dedup and everything downstream
key on the product id. `builtin_qemu` ("qemu"/"qemu") is unaffected.

**Static prose** (the non-discovery sites):
- `main.cpp:56` tagline -> drop "Verilator" (e.g. "Multi-engine driver for the
  Andes simulators (QEMU + vsim).").
- `main.cpp:73` `--engine` example -> `vsim:ax45mpv_premium`.
- `models.hpp:23,25,26` (the `list models` ENGINES/NOTES cells) -> `vsim`.

**Load-bearing test filter:** `plan_itest.cpp:36` filters discovered engines by
`e.type == "verilator"` -> change to `"vsim"` (discovered engines are now vsim).

Leave: in-source code comments, and every **real filesystem path** (`verilator/build`,
`verilator/CMakeLists.txt`, `VSIM_VERILATOR_EXECUTABLE`) - those name the on-disk
submodule / the actual tool, not the product engine label.

## Change B - release/dev tiers

In `driver/main.cpp` only:
- `Subcommand` gains `Tier tier;`; tag each entry per the table above.
- `print_usage`: iterate Release entries; if `ANDES_SIM_DEV` is set (a small
  `is_dev_mode()` = `getenv("ANDES_SIM_DEV")` non-empty), print a
  `developer commands:` section of Dev entries; else print the hint line.
- Dispatch (`main.cpp:116-119`) unchanged. `build`/`doctor` still run; `test` +
  the Hidden five still fall through to "not yet implemented".

## Tests (strict TDD: RED first, then implement)

**1. Normalization (unit) - extend `driver/run_test.cpp`** (already includes
   `engine_registry.hpp`; no new target, no CMake change):
   - RED: assert `normalize_engine_label` maps `{type:"verilator",
     id:"verilator:ax45mpv_premium"}` -> `{vsim, vsim:ax45mpv_premium}`; leaves
     `qemu`/`qemu` and a non-verilator type (`alioth:x`) untouched. Fails to
     compile until the helper exists.
   - GREEN: add the inline helper; wire the `scan_dir` call.

**2. Release surface (acceptance) - new
   `tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_release_surface.sh`** (shell, guarded like the
   other `tests/andes_sim/*` scripts, sources `tests/lib/log.sh`):
   - RED (run against the current binary first to show it fails):
     - `--help`: matches `run`,`list`; does NOT match
       `build|test|doctor|profile|cluster|archive|replay|estimate`; does NOT
       match `-i verilator`; matches the dev hint.
     - `ANDES_SIM_DEV=1 --help`: matches `build`,`test`,`doctor`; still no
       `verilator`; still no `profile|cluster|...`.
     - `run --help`: matches `vsim:`, not `verilator:`.
     - `list models`: no `verilator`, has `vsim`.
     - `list engines` via a fake `ANDES_SIM_ENGINES_DIR` engine that
       self-describes `"type":"verilator"` (reuse the `mkengine` pattern from
       `test_andes_sim_f8.sh`): output shows `vsim:`, never `verilator` -> proves
       the normalization end to end, deterministically, no real sim_* needed.
   - GREEN: implement A + B, rebuild, rerun -> all green.

**3. Update existing tests to the vsim contract** (the id contract changed; tests
   that encode the old label move with it):
   - Must change (discovery renames them, else they break): `test_andes_sim_f2.sh`,
     `test_andes_sim_f3.sh`, `test_andes_sim_f8.sh` (fake-engine ids + the
     `'no engine ...'` / `'multiple cycle-accurate ...'` greps), and the
     `ENG=` var in `test_andes_sim_f9.sh`.
   - Consistency (still pass, but should not show a stale label): the
     `--engine verilator:*` / id literals in `cli_test.cpp`, `run_test.cpp`,
     `plan_test.cpp`, `test_andes_sim_f7.sh`, and `json_test.cpp`'s sample
     descriptor.
   - Leave real-path refs (`verilator/build/sim_*`, `verilator/CMakeLists.txt`).

## Docs

`docs/USER_GUIDE.md`: update the **CLI-surface** references only - the command
listing, any `--engine`/engine-id example, and the `list engines` sample output
-> `vsim`. Leave the build/setup sections that legitimately discuss Verilator the
tool and the `verilator/` submodule path (lines ~87,114,177,231,285,297,303,309).

## Key files

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `driver/engine_registry.hpp` | NEW inline `normalize_engine_label` |
| `driver/engine_registry.cpp` | call it in `scan_dir` before dedup |
| `driver/main.cpp` | `Tier` enum + field; tier-filtered `print_usage` + dev reveal; tagline/`--engine` prose |
| `driver/models.hpp` | `list models` cells -> `vsim` |
| `driver/run_test.cpp` | RED: normalize unit cases (+ id-literal consistency) |
| `driver/plan_itest.cpp` | `type=="vsim"` filter |
| `tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_release_surface.sh` | NEW acceptance |
| `tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_f{2,3,8,9,7}.sh` | ids/greps -> `vsim` |
| `driver/{cli,plan,json}_test.cpp` | id-literal consistency |
| `docs/USER_GUIDE.md` | CLI-surface refs -> `vsim` |

## Reuse
`resolve_accurate_engine` inline pattern (model for the new inline helper),
`mkengine` fake-engine pattern (`test_andes_sim_f8.sh`), `expect`/`fail`/`ok`
(`tests/lib/log.sh`), `discover_engines`/`scan_dir` (the single seam).

## Verification
- Build: `bash scripts/build_driver.sh`
- Unit (RED then GREEN): `./build/driver/andes-sim-run-test`
- Acceptance: `bash tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_release_surface.sh`
- Regression (vsim contract): `bash tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_f2.sh`,
  `...f3.sh`, `...f8.sh`; and the full driver unit set
  (`for t in cli plan json run elf-syms hybrid; do ./build/driver/andes-sim-$t-test; done`)
- Manual smoke:
  `./build/andes-sim --help`  (only run/list + hint),
  `ANDES_SIM_DEV=1 ./build/andes-sim --help`  (adds build/test/doctor),
  `./build/andes-sim list engines`  (vsim: ids, no "verilator")

## Commit split (when you later ask to commit)
Two behavioral units, each with its tests: (1) verilator->vsim rename +
normalization; (2) release/dev tiering. The `Tier` enum/field is introduced with
its tagging in unit (2) - no separate structural commit is warranted (it changes
output immediately).

# andes-sim release surface: hide "verilator", split release vs dev commands

## Context

`andes-sim` is the release product, but `--help` today exposes implementation
detail and unfinished work. Looking at `./build/andes-sim --help` the user (PM)
asked for four things:

1. Hide the word **verilator** from users (it shows in the `--help` tagline, the
   `--engine` example, `list models`, and the whole `list engines` TYPE column +
   ids like `verilator:ax45mpv_premium`).
2. Don't output **unfinished** features (`estimate`, `cluster`, `profile`, and
   the like).
3. **Separate** release features from development features.
4. The release product **shouldn't include `build` and `test`**.

Today the command table (`driver/main.cpp:35-46`) lists all 10 commands and the
help printer shows every one. Engine identity ("verilator") comes from the vsim
binary's `--describe` JSON; the driver passes it through verbatim. Selection
keys off `kind=="cycle-accurate"`, never the `type` string (`engine_registry.hpp:45`),
so relabeling the engine is safe.

Outcome: a clean release surface (`run`, `list`) that never says "verilator",
with `build`/`test`/`doctor` reachable to developers via an env var, and the
half-built ROADMAP commands hidden until they land.

## Decisions (locked)

- Replace "verilator" with **`vsim`** everywhere on the surface: TYPE column
  `vsim`, ids `vsim:ax45mpv_premium`, `--engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium`.
- Scrub **everywhere incl. ids** (one normalization point at discovery flips
  list / `--engine` / errors / banner together).
- Reveal dev commands via **`ANDES_SIM_DEV=1`** (release `--help` stays clean +
  one hint line; the env var adds a "developer commands" section).

**Inference to confirm at approval:** `doctor` -> **dev tier** (not release). Its
content is entirely build/setup (submodules, toolchain, `./hsim build`) and it is
the only Release command that would still print real `verilator/` paths
(`cmd_doctor.cpp:60,110`) which cannot be renamed. So Release = `run` + `list`.

## Command tiers (the one new idea)

Add `enum class Tier { Release, Dev, Hidden }` + a field on `Subcommand`
(`main.cpp:28-31`). `print_usage` shows Release; appends a Dev section only when
`ANDES_SIM_DEV` is set; Hidden is never listed. Dispatch is unchanged, so the
command surface stays stable (matches the file's stated F0 design intent).

| Tier | Commands | `--help` behavior |
|------|----------|-------------------|
| Release | `run`, `list` | always listed |
| Dev | `build`, `test`, `doctor` | listed only under `ANDES_SIM_DEV=1` |
| Hidden | `profile`, `cluster`, `archive`, `replay`, `estimate` | never listed; explicit invocation still hits the existing "not yet implemented" stub |

Not in dev mode, the release help ends with one hint line:
`(set ANDES_SIM_DEV=1 to show developer commands)`.

## Change A - hide "verilator" -> "vsim"

**Single normalization point.** Add an inline helper in
`driver/engine_registry.hpp` (mirroring the existing inline `resolve_accurate_engine`):

```cpp
inline void normalize_engine_label(EngineDescriptor& d) {
  // The vsim binary self-reports the third-party simulator name; the product
  // surface speaks "vsim". One translation point so every downstream consumer
  // (list / --engine / errors / banner) sees the product id.
  if (d.type == "verilator") d.type = "vsim";
  if (d.id.rfind("verilator:", 0) == 0) d.id = "vsim:" + d.id.substr(10);
}
```

Call it in `engine_registry.cpp` `scan_dir`, right after `describe_one` succeeds
and **before** the `seen.insert(d.id)` dedup, so dedup and everything downstream
key on the product id. `builtin_qemu` ("qemu"/"qemu") is unaffected.

**Static prose** (the non-discovery sites):
- `main.cpp:56` tagline -> drop "Verilator" (e.g. "Multi-engine driver for the
  Andes simulators (QEMU + vsim).").
- `main.cpp:73` `--engine` example -> `vsim:ax45mpv_premium`.
- `models.hpp:23,25,26` (the `list models` ENGINES/NOTES cells) -> `vsim`.

**Load-bearing test filter:** `plan_itest.cpp:36` filters discovered engines by
`e.type == "verilator"` -> change to `"vsim"` (discovered engines are now vsim).

Leave: in-source code comments, and every **real filesystem path** (`verilator/build`,
`verilator/CMakeLists.txt`, `VSIM_VERILATOR_EXECUTABLE`) - those name the on-disk
submodule / the actual tool, not the product engine label.

In `driver/main.cpp` only:
- `Subcommand` gains `Tier tier;`; tag each entry per the table above.

# F9 - `run --model hybrid` (csr | pc | icount triggers)

## Context

F9 is the next ROADMAP feature (F0-F8 done). Today `andes-sim run --model hybrid`
prints `not yet implemented`. The goal: orchestrate a real QEMU1 -> vsim handoff
for the three kernel/window triggers and print the cycle figure - matching the
Python golden `hsim`'s numbers, and replacing its `tests/e2e.sh` delegation.

Good news: **F6 already does the hard part.** `run_plan` (driver/run_plan.cpp)
spawns `[qemu fast-leg -> vsim accurate-leg]`, threads the drained
`hybrid_state_v1`, and reads each leg's `mcycle`. `plan_itest.cpp` proves the
**csr** trigger runs end-to-end and `vsim_mcycle > qemu_mcycle`. So F9 is mostly:
teach the plan the **pc** and **icount** trigger args, port the ELF symbol
lookup, add the CLI flags, and wire `cmd_run` to build+run the plan and print.

Golden behavior I verified directly (real `hsim`, not the hallucinated `hsim.py`):
- QEMU leg (all triggers): `-object memory-backend-file...` + `-plugin {plugin},outfile={state},<trig>`, exits 200. (`hsim:725-755`, `e2e.sh:111-118`)
- vsim leg: `{elf} --resume-from-qemu {in} --handoff-out {out} --shared-mem-{path,size,base} <trig>`, exits 200. (`e2e.sh:134-142`)
- Trigger args: **csr** none; **pc** plugin `,enter_pc=0x<start>` + vsim `--hybrid-exit-pc 0x<end>`; **icount** plugin `,icount=<N>` + vsim `--hybrid-icount <M>`. (`e2e.sh:85-89`, `hsim:275,361`)
- Cycle line: `[<label> window_cycles] <V-Q>  (vsim mcycle=<V> - qemu mcycle=<Q>)`. (`hsim:465`)
- pc boundary = symbol name or `0x` addr, resolved against the ELF symtab. (`tests/lib/roi.sh:15-21`)
- Defaults: qemu-icount 10000, vsim-icount 5000, mmap 128 MiB. (`hsim:1304-1342`)

## Core architecture (the one new idea: trigger -> per-leg argv)

Everything else reuses F6. A trigger contributes args to each leg, **chosen by
the leg's role**:


# andes-sim release surface: hide "verilator", split release vs dev commands

## Context

`andes-sim` is the release product, but `--help` today exposes implementation
detail and unfinished work. Looking at `./build/andes-sim --help` the user (PM)
asked for four things:

1. Hide the word **verilator** from users (it shows in the `--help` tagline, the
   `--engine` example, `list models`, and the whole `list engines` TYPE column +
   ids like `verilator:ax45mpv_premium`).
2. Don't output **unfinished** features (`estimate`, `cluster`, `profile`, and
   the like).
3. **Separate** release features from development features.
4. The release product **shouldn't include `build` and `test`**.

Today the command table (`driver/main.cpp:35-46`) lists all 10 commands and the
help printer shows every one. Engine identity ("verilator") comes from the vsim
binary's `--describe` JSON; the driver passes it through verbatim. Selection
keys off `kind=="cycle-accurate"`, never the `type` string (`engine_registry.hpp:45`),
so relabeling the engine is safe.

Outcome: a clean release surface (`run`, `list`) that never says "verilator",
with `build`/`test`/`doctor` reachable to developers via an env var, and the
half-built ROADMAP commands hidden until they land.

## Decisions (locked)

- Replace "verilator" with **`vsim`** everywhere on the surface: TYPE column
  `vsim`, ids `vsim:ax45mpv_premium`, `--engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium`.
- Scrub **everywhere incl. ids** (one normalization point at discovery flips
  list / `--engine` / errors / banner together).
- Reveal dev commands via **`ANDES_SIM_DEV=1`** (release `--help` stays clean +
  one hint line; the env var adds a "developer commands" section).

**Inference to confirm at approval:** `doctor` -> **dev tier** (not release). Its
content is entirely build/setup (submodules, toolchain, `./hsim build`) and it is
the only Release command that would still print real `verilator/` paths
(`cmd_doctor.cpp:60,110`) which cannot be renamed. So Release = `run` + `list`.

## Command tiers (the one new idea)

Add `enum class Tier { Release, Dev, Hidden }` + a field on `Subcommand`
(`main.cpp:28-31`). `print_usage` shows Release; appends a Dev section only when
`ANDES_SIM_DEV` is set; Hidden is never listed. Dispatch is unchanged, so the
command surface stays stable (matches the file's stated F0 design intent).

| Tier | Commands | `--help` behavior |
|------|----------|-------------------|
| Release | `run`, `list` | always listed |
| Dev | `build`, `test`, `doctor` | listed only under `ANDES_SIM_DEV=1` |
| Hidden | `profile`, `cluster`, `archive`, `replay`, `estimate` | never listed; explicit invocation still hits the existing "not yet implemented" stub |

Not in dev mode, the release help ends with one hint line:
`(set ANDES_SIM_DEV=1 to show developer commands)`.

## Change A - hide "verilator" -> "vsim"

**Single normalization point.** Add an inline helper in
`driver/engine_registry.hpp` (mirroring the existing inline `resolve_accurate_engine`):

```cpp
inline void normalize_engine_label(EngineDescriptor& d) {
  // The vsim binary self-reports the third-party simulator name; the product
  // surface speaks "vsim". One translation point so every downstream consumer
  // (list / --engine / errors / banner) sees the product id.
  if (d.type == "verilator") d.type = "vsim";
  if (d.id.rfind("verilator:", 0) == 0) d.id = "vsim:" + d.id.substr(10);
}
```

Call it in `engine_registry.cpp` `scan_dir`, right after `describe_one` succeeds
and **before** the `seen.insert(d.id)` dedup, so dedup and everything downstream
key on the product id. `builtin_qemu` ("qemu"/"qemu") is unaffected.

**Static prose** (the non-discovery sites):
- `main.cpp:56` tagline -> drop "Verilator" (e.g. "Multi-engine driver for the
  Andes simulators (QEMU + vsim).").
- `main.cpp:73` `--engine` example -> `vsim:ax45mpv_premium`.
- `models.hpp:23,25,26` (the `list models` ENGINES/NOTES cells) -> `vsim`.

**Load-bearing test filter:** `plan_itest.cpp:36` filters discovered engines by
`e.type == "verilator"` -> change to `"vsim"` (discovered engines are now vsim).

Leave: in-source code comments, and every **real filesystem path** (`verilator/build`,
`verilator/CMakeLists.txt`, `VSIM_VERILATOR_EXECUTABLE`) - those name the on-disk
submodule / the actual tool, not the product engine label.

## Change B - release/dev tiers

In `driver/main.cpp` only:
- `Subcommand` gains `Tier tier;`; tag each entry per the table above.
- `print_usage`: iterate Release entries; if `ANDES_SIM_DEV` is set (a small
  `is_dev_mode()` = `getenv("ANDES_SIM_DEV")` non-empty), print a
  `developer commands:` section of Dev entries; else print the hint line.
- Dispatch (`main.cpp:116-119`) unchanged. `build`/`doctor` still run; `test` +
  the Hidden five still fall through to "not yet implemented".

## Tests (strict TDD: RED first, then implement)

**1. Normalization (unit) - extend `driver/run_test.cpp`** (already includes
   `engine_registry.hpp`; no new target, no CMake change):
   - RED: assert `normalize_engine_label` maps `{type:"verilator",
     id:"verilator:ax45mpv_premium"}` -> `{vsim, vsim:ax45mpv_premium}`; leaves
     `qemu`/`qemu` and a non-verilator type (`alioth:x`) untouched. Fails to
     compile until the helper exists.
   - GREEN: add the inline helper; wire the `scan_dir` call.

**2. Release surface (acceptance) - new
   `tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_release_surface.sh`** (shell, guarded like the
   other `tests/andes_sim/*` scripts, sources `tests/lib/log.sh`):
   - RED (run against the current binary first to show it fails):
     - `--help`: matches `run`,`list`; does NOT match
       `build|test|doctor|profile|cluster|archive|replay|estimate`; does NOT
       match `-i verilator`; matches the dev hint.
     - `ANDES_SIM_DEV=1 --help`: matches `build`,`test`,`doctor`; still no
       `verilator`; still no `profile|cluster|...`.
     - `run --help`: matches `vsim:`, not `verilator:`.
     - `list models`: no `verilator`, has `vsim`.
     - `list engines` via a fake `ANDES_SIM_ENGINES_DIR` engine that
       self-describes `"type":"verilator"` (reuse the `mkengine` pattern from
       `test_andes_sim_f8.sh`): output shows `vsim:`, never `verilator` -> proves
       the normalization end to end, deterministically, no real sim_* needed.
   - GREEN: implement A + B, rebuild, rerun -> all green.

**3. Update existing tests to the vsim contract** (the id contract changed; tests
   that encode the old label move with it):
   - Must change (discovery renames them, else they break): `test_andes_sim_f2.sh`,
     `test_andes_sim_f3.sh`, `test_andes_sim_f8.sh` (fake-engine ids + the
     `'no engine ...'` / `'multiple cycle-accurate ...'` greps), and the
     `ENG=` var in `test_andes_sim_f9.sh`.
   - Consistency (still pass, but should not show a stale label): the
     `--engine verilator:*` / id literals in `cli_test.cpp`, `run_test.cpp`,
     `plan_test.cpp`, `test_andes_sim_f7.sh`, and `json_test.cpp`'s sample
     descriptor.
   - Leave real-path refs (`verilator/build/sim_*`, `verilator/CMakeLists.txt`).

## Docs

`docs/USER_GUIDE.md`: update the **CLI-surface** references only - the command
listing, any `--engine`/engine-id example, and the `list engines` sample output
-> `vsim`. Leave the build/setup sections that legitimately discuss Verilator the
tool and the `verilator/` submodule path (lines ~87,114,177,231,285,297,303,309).

## Key files

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `driver/engine_registry.hpp` | NEW inline `normalize_engine_label` |
| `driver/engine_registry.cpp` | call it in `scan_dir` before dedup |
| `driver/main.cpp` | `Tier` enum + field; tier-filtered `print_usage` + dev reveal; tagline/`--engine` prose |
| `driver/models.hpp` | `list models` cells -> `vsim` |
| `driver/run_test.cpp` | RED: normalize unit cases (+ id-literal consistency) |
| `driver/plan_itest.cpp` | `type=="vsim"` filter |
| `tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_release_surface.sh` | NEW acceptance |
| `tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_f{2,3,8,9,7}.sh` | ids/greps -> `vsim` |
| `driver/{cli,plan,json}_test.cpp` | id-literal consistency |
| `docs/USER_GUIDE.md` | CLI-surface refs -> `vsim` |

## Reuse
`resolve_accurate_engine` inline pattern (model for the new inline helper),
`mkengine` fake-engine pattern (`test_andes_sim_f8.sh`), `expect`/`fail`/`ok`
(`tests/lib/log.sh`), `discover_engines`/`scan_dir` (the single seam).

## Verification
- Build: `bash scripts/build_driver.sh`
- Unit (RED then GREEN): `./build/driver/andes-sim-run-test`
- Acceptance: `bash tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_release_surface.sh`
- Regression (vsim contract): `bash tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_f2.sh`,
  `...f3.sh`, `...f8.sh`; and the full driver unit set
  (`for t in cli plan json run elf-syms hybrid; do ./build/driver/andes-sim-$t-test; done`)
- Manual smoke:
  `./build/andes-sim --help`  (only run/list + hint),
  `ANDES_SIM_DEV=1 ./build/andes-sim --help`  (adds build/test/doctor),
  `./build/andes-sim list engines`  (vsim: ids, no "verilator")

## Commit split (when you later ask to commit)
Two behavioral units, each with its tests: (1) verilator->vsim rename +
normalization; (2) release/dev tiering. The `Tier` enum/field is introduced with
its tagging in unit (2) - no separate structural commit is warranted (it changes
output immediately).

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Release-surface contract: the andes-sim PRODUCT help shows only the finished,
# user-facing commands (run, list) and never the third-party simulator name
# "verilator". Developer commands (build, test, doctor) appear only under
# ANDES_SIM_DEV=1; the unfinished ROADMAP commands (profile, cluster, archive,
# replay, estimate) appear in no help at all. The cycle-accurate engine is
# presented as "vsim" everywhere -- proven end to end with a fake engine that
# self-describes as "verilator" and must come back out as vsim:.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

BIN="$ROOT/build/andes-sim"

bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"

# has RE TEXT  -- TEXT must match RE ; missing RE TEXT -- TEXT must NOT match RE
has()     { printf '%s\n' "$2" | grep -Eq "$1"; }
no_word() { ! printf '%s\n' "$2" | grep -qi 'verilator'; }

# 1. release --help: run + list only, the dev hint, and no "verilator".
H=$("$BIN" --help 2>&1)
has '^  run '  "$H" || fail "release --help: missing 'run'"
has '^  list ' "$H" || fail "release --help: missing 'list'"
for c in build test doctor profile cluster archive replay estimate; do
  has "^  $c " "$H" && fail "release --help: leaked non-release command '$c'"
done
no_word "$H" || fail "release --help: leaked 'verilator'"
has 'ANDES_SIM_DEV' "$H" || fail "release --help: missing developer-commands hint"
ok "release --help: run/list only, dev hint, no verilator"

# 2. ANDES_SIM_DEV=1 --help: adds build/test/doctor; hidden five stay hidden.
D=$(ANDES_SIM_DEV=1 "$BIN" --help 2>&1)
for c in run list build test doctor; do
  has "^  $c " "$D" || fail "dev --help: missing '$c'"
done
for c in profile cluster archive replay estimate; do
  has "^  $c " "$D" && fail "dev --help: leaked hidden command '$c'"
done
no_word "$D" || fail "dev --help: leaked 'verilator'"
ok "dev --help: adds build/test/doctor, hidden cmds stay hidden, no verilator"

# 3. run --help: the --engine example reads vsim:, never verilator:.
RH=$("$BIN" run --help 2>&1)
has 'vsim:' "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing vsim: example"
no_word "$RH" || fail "run --help: leaked 'verilator'"
ok "run --help: vsim: example, no verilator"

# 4. list models: the composition cells read vsim, never verilator.
LM=$("$BIN" list models 2>&1)
has 'vsim' "$LM" || fail "list models: missing vsim"
no_word "$LM" || fail "list models: leaked 'verilator'"
ok "list models: vsim, no verilator"

# 5. list engines end to end: a fake engine that self-describes as "verilator"
# must surface as vsim: (the single normalization point), proving --engine /
# errors / list all speak the product name with no real sim_* needed.
TMP=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT
cat >"$TMP/sim_fake" <<'EOF'
#!/bin/sh
[ "$1" = "--describe" ] && printf '%s\n' '{"id":"verilator:fakecfg","type":"verilator","kind":"cycle-accurate","vlen":256,"xlen":64,"triggers":["csr","pc","icount"],"roles":["standalone","accurate-leg"],"state":["resume","drain"],"invoke":{"standalone":["{bin}","{elf}"]},"result":"stderr:cycles"}'
EOF
chmod +x "$TMP/sim_fake"
LE=$(ANDES_SIM_ENGINES_DIR="$TMP" "$BIN" list engines 2>&1)
has 'vsim:fakecfg' "$LE" || fail "list engines: fake not renamed to vsim:fakecfg:"$'\n'"$LE"
no_word "$LE" || fail "list engines: leaked 'verilator':"$'\n'"$LE"
ok "list engines: a verilator-self-describing engine is shown as vsim:"

ok "release surface (hide verilator + release/dev command split)"

#!/usr/bin/env bash

#   1. JSON parser unit tests pass.

#   3. a self-describing engine in the scan dir is discovered (--describe).
#   4. its kind / vlen / triggers show in `list engines`.
#   5. HOT-PLUG: dropping a second engine in makes it appear with no rebuild.
#   6. SIDECAR fallback: a binary lacking --describe is read from <bin>.json.

# the default verilator/build scan), so the real multi-MB sim binaries are
# never executed here.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

JSONTEST="$ROOT/build/driver/andes-sim-json-test"

bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"
[ -x "$BIN" ] || fail "missing executable: $BIN"

# 1. JSON parser unit tests
[ -x "$JSONTEST" ] || fail "missing json unit-test binary: $JSONTEST"
"$JSONTEST" >/dev/null || fail "json unit tests failed"

# A self-describing fake engine: emits a descriptor on --describe, else fails.
make_engine() {  # $1=path  $2=id  $3=vlen
  cat > "$1" <<OUTER
#!/usr/bin/env bash
if [ "\$1" = "--describe" ]; then
  printf '%s\n' '{"id":"$2","type":"verilator","kind":"cycle-accurate","vlen":$3,"xlen":64,"triggers":["csr","pc","icount"],"roles":["standalone","accurate-leg"],"state":["resume","drain"],"invoke":{"standalone":["{bin}","{elf}"]},"result":"stderr:cycles"}'
  exit 0
fi
exit 1
OUTER
  chmod +x "$1"
}

ENGDIR=$(mktemp -d -t andes-f2.XXXXXX)
trap 'rm -rf "$ENGDIR"' EXIT

make_engine "$ENGDIR/sim_fakeA" "verilator:fakeA" 256

echo "$out" | grep -q "verilator:fakeA" || fail "fakeA not discovered:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -q "256" || fail "fakeA vlen (256) not shown:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -q "cycle-accurate" || fail "fakeA kind not shown:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -q "csr" || fail "fakeA triggers not shown:"$'\n'"$out"
